mainTopic: The words around קריאת שמע (אמת, פרשת ציצית at night, יציאת מצרים), the order of its פרשיות, and saying שמע together with תפילין
overview: This amud starts with the word אמת after קריאת שמע. רבי יוחנן says one repeats אמת to open the next ברכה, while רבה says once is enough. Next comes a custom from ארץ ישראל of saying only the start and end of פרשת ציצית at night, which אביי challenges and רב פפא defends. אביי concludes that in בבל we say the whole פרשה at night. חייא בר רב rules that after 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' one must say אמת, and someone who skips both says a short 'מודים' text so that he still mentions יציאת מצרים. The גמרא then explains why פרשת שמע comes first: to accept עול מלכות שמים before עול מצוות, and because it contains learning, teaching and doing. A story about רב saying שמע before putting on תפילין leads to a long back-and-forth, which ends with the explanation that his messenger brought the תפילין late. The amud closes with עולא and רבי יוחנן stressing how important it is to wear תפילין during שמע, and רבי יוחנן's teaching on complete acceptance of Heaven's kingship continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse that joins 'ה׳ אלהיכם' to 'אמת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ירמיהו that puts אמת right next to God's name. This explains why the end of קריאת שמע ('ה׳ אלהיכם') must flow straight into 'אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And ה׳, God, is Truth."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source for the previous discussion. That discussion taught that you should not stop between the last words of קריאת שמע ('ה׳ אלהיכם') and the word אמת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word אמת is attached directly to God's name. So in davening, 'ה׳ אלהיכם' and 'אמת' are treated as one unit that should not be split. This also sets up the next question: if אמת is already attached to the end of קריאת שמע, does one need to say it again?

keyTerms.meaning: Truth; also the first word of the ברכה after קריאת שמע
"And ה׳, God, is Truth" (ירמיהו י:י)
The recitation of the שמע

steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק is not starting a brand-new topic. It finishes the previous point from the previous amud (14a): the reason we don't interrupt between 'ה׳ אלהיכם' and 'אמת'.

phrases.english: "And ה׳, God, is Truth."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו י:י. Proof that אמת is attached to God's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the rule (earlier) not to pause between 'ה׳ אלהיכם' and 'אמת'.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that 'ה׳ אלהיכם' and 'אמת' should be said together without interruption.

steps.title: Does one say אמת a second time?
steps.stepSummary: The person has already said 'ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'. Does he repeat אמת as the first word of the ברכה of אמת ויציב?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he go back and say 'אמת' again, or does he not go back and say 'אמת' again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that sets up the next two opinions. The word אמת was already said attached to 'ה׳ אלהיכם'. Is it said again to open the ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אמת is doing two jobs: it closes קריאת שמע and it opens the ברכה of אמת ויציב. The question is whether that one word is enough for both jobs, or whether the ברכה needs its own אמת.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes back and says (again)
The ברכה said right after קריאת שמע in the morning

phrases.english: Does he go back and say 'Emet'?
phrases.notes: Option 1: say אמת a second time.

phrases.english: Or does he not go back and say 'Emet'?
phrases.notes: Option 2: the first אמת covers both.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר ״אֱמֶת״, אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר ״אֱמֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that אמת is attached to 'ה׳ אלהיכם', and asks whether a second אמת is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the word אמת is repeated at the start of the ברכה after it was already said at the end of קריאת שמע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Say it again
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that one does repeat אמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: He goes back and says 'אמת' again.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: according to רבי יוחנן, you say אמת twice. Once at the end of קריאת שמע, and once to begin the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן treats the ברכה as needing its own opening word. The first אמת belongs to קריאת שמע, so the ברכה must start with a fresh אמת.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who transmits רבי יוחנן's teaching
Leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: Attribution chain.

phrases.english: He goes back and says 'Emet' again.
phrases.notes: Repeat the word.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One repeats אמת to open the ברכה.

steps.title: רבה: Do not say it again
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees and says one does not repeat אמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: He does not go back and say 'אמת' again.
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer: רבה holds that saying אמת once is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the single אמת said after 'ה׳ אלהיכם' serves both as the end of קריאת שמע and as the start of the ברכה. Saying it again would be unnecessary repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonian אמורא, head of the ישיבה in פומבדיתא
He does not go back (repeat)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions. רבי יוחנן: say אמת twice. רבה: say it once, and it counts for both.

phrases.english: Rabba said: He does not go back and say 'Emet' again.
phrases.notes: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבה teases a חזן who said 'אמת, אמת'
steps.stepSummary: A חזן davened before רבה and said 'אמת, אמת' twice. רבה joked that this man must be truly gripped by truth, showing he held the repetition unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down to lead the prayers before רבה. רבה heard him say 'אמת, אמת' two times. רבה said: Every 'אמת, אמת' has seized this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows רבה's opinion in real life. When a חזן repeated אמת, רבה made a mocking remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's sarcastic line ('this one is grabbed by all the truth!') shows he really did think repeating אמת is wrong. The story confirms that רבה's ruling was his actual practice, not just a theory.

keyTerms.meaning: Who went down before him (to lead the prayer as חזן)
Two times
Has seized/caught this one

steps.confusionAlert: 'Went down' does not mean he left. In the time of the גמרא the חזן stood in a lower spot in front of the ark, so 'going down' means going up to lead davening.

phrases.english: A certain man went down (to lead prayer) before Rabba.
phrases.notes: He served as חזן.

phrases.english: Rabba heard him say
'Emet, Emet' two times.
phrases.notes: He followed the practice of repeating.

phrases.english: Rabba said: Every 'Emet, Emet' has seized this one!
phrases.notes: Sarcastic remark: he is overflowing with truth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבה's opinion through his reaction to a חזן.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that one does not repeat אמת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the חזן who said 'אמת, אמת' and רבה's mocking reply.

steps.title: רב יוסף praises a tradition from ארץ ישראל about the evening קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף praises a tradition that רב שמואל בר יהודה brought from ארץ ישראל. At night, they said only the beginning and end of the ציצית פרשה, ending with 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How excellent is this teaching! When רב שמואל בר יהודה came (from ארץ ישראל) he said: In the West (ארץ ישראל), at night they say: 'Speak to the children of Israel and say to them... I am ה׳ your God, אמת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new report about how they said קריאת שמע at night in ארץ ישראל. The גמרא is setting up a discussion of this practice, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third פרשה of שמע (ציצית) is about a מצוה that applies by day. So in ארץ ישראל at night they said only its opening line and its closing words. They still ended with 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת', keeping אמת attached to God's name. The גמרא will soon question what is so 'excellent' about this.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonian אמורא, colleague and successor of רבה
How excellent is this teaching!
'In the West': ארץ ישראל
The evening prayer / at night
The third פרשה of קריאת שמע

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted line skips from the first פסוק of the ציצית פרשה straight to its last words. They did not say the whole פרשה at night.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כַּמָּה מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: How excellent is this teaching,
phrases.notes: Praise that the גמרא will question next.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אֲמַר:
phrases.english: For when Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: In the West, at the evening prayer, they say:
phrases.notes: The practice in ארץ ישראל at night.

phrases.english: "Speak to the children of Israel
phrases.notes: במדבר טו:לח, the opening of the ציצית פרשה.

phrases.english: and say to them
phrases.notes: Here they skip ahead to the end.

phrases.english: I am ה׳ your God, Emet."
phrases.notes: במדבר טו:מא, the closing words, with אמת attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כַּמָּה מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a related tradition about the evening קריאת שמע that also ends with 'ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל at night they recited an abbreviated ציצית פרשה: its opening words and its closing 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.

steps.title: אביי challenges the praised custom of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what is so excellent about the custom of ארץ ישראל. רב said that one should not begin פרשת ציצית at night, but if he begins, he must finish it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is so good about it? Didn't רב כהנא say in the name of רב: One should not begin, but if he began, he finishes?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the custom that רב יוסף just praised. He uses a rule of רב that seems to forbid starting the פרשה and then stopping partway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule has two parts. First, at night you should not begin פרשת ציצית at all. Second, if you do begin, you must finish it. The custom of ארץ ישראל begins the פרשה and skips to the end, so it seems to break the second part of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the excellence? What is so good about it?
He should not begin (פרשת ציצית at night)
And if he began, he finishes
But didn't [so-and-so] say? A standard opening for a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The 'him' in 'אביי said to him' is רב יוסף, who praised the custom in the previous step. אביי was רב יוסף's student, and here he questions his teacher's praise.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rav Yosef):
What is so excellent about it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Kahana say in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: The source used for the challenge.

phrases.english: One should not begin (the tzitzis portion at night),
but if he began, he finishes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְעַלְּיוּתָא? וְהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the custom of ארץ ישראל that רב יוסף praised in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The custom of ארץ ישראל of saying only the beginning and end of פרשת ציצית at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that once you begin the פרשה you must finish it. The custom begins it and does not finish it, so it seems to contradict רב.

steps.title: אביי closes off a possible escape
steps.stepSummary: אביי anticipates a defense: maybe the words they said in ארץ ישראל do not count as 'beginning' the פרשה. He blocks it with another teaching of רב, which says that "ואמרת אליהם" does count as a beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that "And say to them" is not considered a beginning, didn't רב שמואל בר יצחק say in the name of רב: "Speak to the children of Israel" is not a beginning, but "And say to them" is a beginning?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי strengthens his own challenge by answering in advance the most obvious defense. The defense would be that the words said in ארץ ישראל were not yet a real start of the פרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many sections of the Torah begin with "דבר אל בני ישראל", so saying those words does not show which פרשה you have started. "ואמרת אליהם" is more specific, and רב says it already counts as starting פרשת ציצית. So the people in ארץ ישראל did begin, and by רב's rule they should have finished.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. Introduces a possible defense that the גמרא then knocks down
A beginning (of the פרשה)
Speak to the children of Israel. A common opening found in many Torah sections
And say to them. The words that follow in פרשת ציצית

phrases.english: And if you will say
that "And say to them" is not considered a beginning

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak say in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: ״דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ לָא הָוֵי הַתְחָלָה,
phrases.english: "Speak to the children of Israel" is not a beginning,
phrases.notes: These words open many Torah sections, so they do not identify this one.

phrases.english: but "And say to them" is a beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא ״וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם״ לָא הָוֵי הַתְחָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge by blocking a defense before anyone can raise it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that the custom of ארץ ישראל never truly 'began' the פרשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself defines "ואמרת אליהם" as a beginning. The custom of ארץ ישראל says those words, so it has begun the פרשה and must finish it.

steps.title: רב פפא: in ארץ ישראל they define the beginning differently
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that in ארץ ישראל they hold that even "ואמרת אליהם" is not yet a beginning. The beginning only comes with "ועשו להם ציצית".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they hold that "And say to them" is also not a beginning, until one says "And they shall make for themselves ציצית."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the custom of ארץ ישראל. He explains that they follow a different definition of when the פרשה 'begins.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not about רב's rule itself. It is about where the 'beginning' of the פרשה falls. In ארץ ישראל only the words about the מצוה itself, "ועשו להם ציצית", count as starting. Since they stopped before those words, they never began, so they did not have to finish.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, in their opinion
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
And they shall make for themselves ציצית. The words that state the actual מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: "מערבא" (the West) is the גמרא's name for ארץ ישראל. It is called 'the West' from the point of view of בבל.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In the West (Eretz Yisrael) they hold
that "And say to them" is also not a beginning
until one says "And they shall make for themselves tzitzis."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Steps 7-8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the custom of ארץ ישראל follows a different definition of 'beginning,' so רב's rule never applied to them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying "ואמרת אליהם" counts as beginning the פרשה, so the custom of ארץ ישראל breaks the rule of 'if he began, he finishes.'
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל the beginning is only at "ועשו להם ציצית". They stopped before that point, so they never began and did not need to finish.

steps.title: אביי's practical rule: we begin, so we finish
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes the practice for בבל. Since ארץ ישראל also begins the פרשה at night, we begin it too, and once we begin, רב's rule requires us to say the whole פרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, we do begin, since they begin in the West. And once we begin, we also finish, as רב כהנא said in the name of רב: One should not begin, but if he began, he finishes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the discussion and turns it into practical halacha for his own community. At night we say the full פרשת ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since even ארץ ישראל says the opening words at night, we feel free to start the פרשה as well. By our own definition, from Steps 7-8, saying "ואמרת אליהם" already counts as a beginning. So רב's rule applies to us: whoever begins must finish, and we say the whole פרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. Introduces a practical conclusion
We do indeed begin
We also do finish

steps.whatToRemember: In בבל (and in our practice) the whole פרשת ציצית is said at night. We begin it, as they do in ארץ ישראל, and רב's rule says that whoever begins must finish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our practice of saying all three פרשיות of שמע, including פרשת ציצית, at מעריב, even though the מצוה of ציצית does not apply at night.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
we do begin (the tzitzis portion at night),
since they begin it in the West (Eretz Yisrael),
and once we have begun,
we also finish it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: For Rav Kahana said in the name of Rav:
One should not begin, but if he began, he finishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב פפא's answer to set the practical custom for בבל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At night we begin פרשת ציצית, and because 'if he began, he finishes,' we say the entire פרשה.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: after saying "אני ה׳ אלהיכם" one must say "אמת"
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב rules that if one said the closing words "אני ה׳ אלהיכם", he must go on to say "אמת". If he did not say "אני ה׳ אלהיכם", he does not need to say "אמת".
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: If one said "I am ה׳ your God," he must say "אמת." If he did not say "I am ה׳ your God," he does not need to say "אמת."
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling links the end of פרשת ציצית to the next ברכה. Finishing with "אני ה׳ אלהיכם" requires continuing with "אמת".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "ה׳ אלהיכם" and "אמת" belong together as one phrase: ה׳ your God is true. So whoever says the closing verse must attach "אמת" to it and continue into the ברכה of אמת ואמונה. Whoever did not say that verse need not say אמת ואמונה at all. The next step challenges this second half.

keyTerms.meaning: I am ה׳ your God. The closing words of פרשת ציצית
He must say "אמת" (and continue with the ברכה)
He does not need to

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
If one said "I am ה׳ your God,"
he must say "Emes" (and continue the blessing).
If he did not say "I am ה׳ your God,"
he does not need to say "Emes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether to say פרשת ציצית at night to how its ending connects to the ברכה of אמת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying "אני ה׳ אלהיכם" requires continuing with "אמת". Without those closing words, there is no such requirement.

steps.title: But they still have to mention leaving Egypt at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second half of חייא בר רב's ruling. If someone did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' and also skips אמת ואמונה, where does he mention יציאת מצרים? That mention is required at night too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he required to mention the going out from Egypt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with חייא בר רב's ruling that someone who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' need not say אמת ואמונה. Without either one, how does he fulfill the duty of mentioning יציאת מצרים at night? The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יציאת מצרים is mentioned in two places: at the end of פרשת ציצית ('אשר הוצאתי אתכם מארץ מצרים') and in the ברכה of אמת ואמונה. A person who skipped פרשת ציצית at night and also skipped אמת ואמונה, as חייא בר רב allows, would leave out every mention of the Exodus. Since that mention is required at night as well, the ruling seems to leave a gap.

keyTerms.meaning: to mention / to bring up
the Exodus, leaving Egypt
but isn't it required…? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: But isn't he required to mention
phrases.notes: וְהָא introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: the going out from Egypt!
phrases.notes: Meaning at night as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second clause of חייא בר רב's ruling in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's ruling that one who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' need not say אמת (ואמונה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning יציאת מצרים at night is required. A person who skipped both the end of פרשת ציצית and אמת ואמונה seems to have never mentioned it.

steps.title: They said a short thanksgiving text that mentions the Exodus
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the person who skipped אמת ואמונה says a short text instead, 'מודים אנחנו לך…'. It thanks ה׳ for taking us out of Egypt, redeeming us, and the miracles at the sea, so it fulfills the mention of יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says like this: 'We thank You, ה׳ our God, that You took us out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed us from the house of slavery, and did for us miracles and mighty acts at the sea, and we sang to You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the person חייא בר רב exempted from אמת ואמונה still mentions יציאת מצרים. He uses a short replacement text instead of אמת ואמונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty is only to mention יציאת מצרים. It does not have to be done with the full ברכה of אמת ואמונה. This short formula covers the Exodus, the redemption, the miracles at the sea, and the song. Those are the same themes found in אמת ואמונה, so the duty is fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: We give thanks to You
and You redeemed us
from the house of slavery
miracles and mighty acts
and we sang

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an extra prayer added on top of everything else. It is a short substitute for אמת ואמונה, said by someone who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם', and it does the job of mentioning יציאת מצרים at night.
steps.whatToRemember: The night-time duty to mention יציאת מצרים can be fulfilled with a short thanksgiving formula. It does not require פרשת ציצית or the full ברכה of אמת ואמונה.

phrases.english: For he says like this:
'We give thanks to You, Lord our God,'
that You took us out of the land of Egypt
and redeemed us from the house of slavery
and performed for us miracles and mighty acts
at the sea, and we sang to You.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 and so defends חייא בר רב's ruling in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the duty was fulfilled with a different text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skipping both 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' and אמת ואמונה means יציאת מצרים is never mentioned at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: In place of אמת ואמונה he says a short 'מודים' formula that mentions יציאת מצרים, so the duty is fulfilled.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: why does שמע come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהושע בן קרחה's question about why פרשת שמע comes before והיה אם שמוע. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: Why did the פרשה of 'שמע' come first, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This step sets up the next move, which brings another explanation for the order of the פרשיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע בן קרחה answers that we first accept עול מלכות שמים and only then עול מצוות. The 'וכו׳' tells us to remember the rest of the משנה. The גמרא quotes it so it can bring a different explanation next.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא quoted in the משנה
came first / preceded
the section / paragraph of
etc., the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
Why did the portion of 'Shema' come first, etc.
phrases.notes: The answer in the משנה: to accept עול מלכות שמים before עול מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה: לָמָּה קָדְמָה פָּרָשַׁת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of the night-time פרשת ציצית and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the פרשיות of שמע has a reason. רבי יהושע בן קרחה explains it as accepting heaven's kingship before the commandments.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: learn, then teach, then do
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different reason for the order. שמע speaks about learning, so it comes before והיה אם שמוע, which speaks about teaching. והיה אם שמוע comes before ויאמר, which speaks about doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: It is right that 'שמע' should come before 'והיה אם שמוע', because this one is for learning and that one is for teaching. And 'והיה אם שמוע' comes before 'ויאמר', because this one is for teaching and that one is for doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן יוחי's own reason for the order of the three פרשיות. His order is learning, then teaching, then doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פרשה, 'ודברת בם' is about learning yourself. In the second, 'ולמדתם אותם את בניכם' is about teaching others. The third, ציצית, is about doing a מצוה. You must learn before you can teach, and you must know before you can do. That is a different logic from רבי יהושע בן קרחה's.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
it is logical / by right
to learn
to teach
to do / perform

steps.confusionAlert: 'Learning' in the first פרשה and 'teaching' in the second can sound alike. The point is that you study for yourself first, and only then pass it on to others.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the order of קריאת שמע. רבי יהושע בן קרחה: the kingship of heaven before the commandments. רבי שמעון בן יוחי: learning, then teaching, then doing.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
It is right that 'Shema' should come first,
before 'VeHaya im Shamoa' —
because this one is for learning, and that one is for teaching.
phrases.notes: 'ודברת בם' versus 'ולמדתם אותם את בניכם'.

phrases.english: And 'VeHaya im Shamoa' before 'VaYomer' —
because this one is for teaching, and that one is for doing.
phrases.notes: The word here is לִלְמוֹד, but in context it means teaching (as Sefaria translates). ויאמר contains the מצוה of ציצית, something you actually do.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: בַּדִּין הוּא שֶׁיַּקְדִּים שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reason, besides the משנה's, for the order of the פרשיות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרשיות are ordered learning, then teaching, then doing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a basic Torah principle: knowledge comes first, then passing it on, then putting it into action.

steps.title: Doesn't שמע also contain teaching and doing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's claim that פרשת שמע is only about learning. That paragraph also says 'teach them', 'bind them', and 'write them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that שמע only has learning in it, and no teaching or doing? But it is written: 'And you shall teach them', 'And you shall bind them', 'And you shall write them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the ברייתא from Step 15. It shows that פרשת שמע clearly contains teaching and doing, not just learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to label each paragraph with only one thing: שמע is learning, והיה אם שמוע is teaching, ויאמר is doing. But ושננתם is a command to teach, and וקשרתם and וכתבתם are commands to do (תפילין and מזוזה). So the one-label-per-paragraph reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)
And you shall teach them (sharply) to your children
And you shall bind them (תפילין)
And you shall write them (מזוזה)

phrases.english: Is that to say that 'Shema' has learning in it,
but it does not have teaching and doing in it?!
But it is written: 'And you shall teach them',
phrases.notes: A command to teach

phrases.english: 'And you shall bind them', 'And you shall write them'!
phrases.notes: Commands to do: תפילין and מזוזה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's description of פרשת שמע
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that פרשת שמע is about learning, as opposed to teaching and doing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses of פרשת שמע themselves contain explicit commands to teach (ושננתם) and to do (וקשרתם, וכתבתם).

steps.title: Doesn't והיה אם שמוע also contain doing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second challenge: והיה אם שמוע also commands actions, such as binding and writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: does והיה אם שמוע only have teaching in it, and no doing? But it is written: 'And you shall bind them', 'And you shall write them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the same ברייתא. This time it targets the second paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said והיה אם שמוע is about teaching, and ויאמר is about doing. But והיה אם שמוע also has וקשרתם and וכתבתם, which are actions. So doing is not unique to ויאמר either.

keyTerms.meaning: And further (a second challenge is coming)
But it is written! (bringing a verse as a challenge)

phrases.english: And further: 'VeHaya im Shamoa' —
is it only teaching that is in it,
and doing is not in it?
But it is written: 'And you shall bind them', 'And you shall write them'!
phrases.notes: Deuteronomy 11:18–20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel challenge to the same ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that והיה אם שמוע contains teaching and not doing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: והיה אם שמוע contains explicit commands to act (וקשרתם, וכתבתם).

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: more kinds of מצוה come first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread. שמע comes first because it has all three: learning, teaching, and doing. והיה אם שמוע has two: teaching and doing. ויאמר has only doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he meant: It is right that שמע comes before והיה אם שמוע, because this one has learning, teaching, and doing. והיה אם שמוע comes before ויאמר, because this one has teaching and doing, while ויאמר has only doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges. It explains that the ברייתא was counting how many kinds of מצוה each paragraph contains, not giving each one a single label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading is a count: שמע has 3 kinds, והיה אם שמוע has 2, ויאמר has 1. The paragraph that holds more comes first. This fits the verses the challenges quoted, so both challenges are resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he meant (rereading a statement)
It is right / logical that
The third paragraph (פרשת ציצית)
Only

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא says ויאמר has no learning value. It means ויאמר's commands are only about doing (ציצית). It has no command to learn or teach.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move. Instead of rejecting a source, it rereads the source so that it fits the verses.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said:
It is right that 'Shema' should come before
'VeHaya im Shamoa',
because this one has learning, teaching, and doing.
'VeHaya im Shamoa' comes before 'VaYomer',
because this one has teaching and doing,
while 'VaYomer' has only doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each paragraph has only one feature: learning, teaching, or doing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each paragraph includes more or fewer features (3, 2, 1), and the order follows that count.

steps.title: Why not just use רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs its own reason when רבי יהושע בן קרחה already explained why שמע comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him derive it from רבי יהושע בן קרחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the ברייתא's reason. רבי יהושע בן קרחה, quoted in the משנה, already gave a reason for the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's reason is that one should first accept עול מלכות שמים and then עול מצוות. If that already explains the order, the ברייתא's count of learning, teaching, and doing seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from... (why not use an existing source?)
The תנא in the משנה who explained the order of the paragraphs

phrases.aramaic: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה!
phrases.english: Let him derive it from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the reread ברייתא's reason is needed at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא's separate reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן קרחה already explained the order, so a second reason looks unnecessary.

steps.title: One reason and another: both are true
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא agrees with רבי יהושע בן קרחה and adds a second reason. First, accept עול מלכות שמים before עול מצוות. Second, שמע contains these other features as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said one reason and another. One: so that a person first accepts the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, and afterward accepts the yoke of the מצוות. And another: because שמע contains these other things too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no argument. The ברייתא gives the reason of רבי יהושע בן קרחה plus an extra one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is the משנה's reason: kingship of ה׳ comes before commandments. Reason two is the ברייתא's count of learning, teaching, and doing. The ברייתא is not replacing the משנה. It is adding a second reason.

keyTerms.meaning: He said one reason and another (an added reason)
Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven: accepting ה׳ as King
Yoke of the מצוות: accepting the commandments
Other matters

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons why שמע comes first. (1) Accept ה׳ as King before accepting His מצוות. (2) שמע contains learning, teaching, and doing, which is more than the other paragraphs.

phrases.english: He said one reason and another,
One: so that he accepts upon himself
the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven first

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: and afterward accepts upon himself the yoke of the מצוות,
and another: because it contains
these other matters.
phrases.notes: Learning, teaching, and doing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by combining both reasons
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additive: an extra reason, not a disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's reason replaces the reason of רבי יהושע בן קרחה, so it seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא accepts the reason of רבי יהושע בן קרחה and adds a second one.

steps.title: רב's morning order: wash, שמע, תפילין, pray
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins with a story. רב washed his hands, said קריאת שמע, then put on תפילין, then prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב washed his hands, recited קריאת שמע, put on תפילין, and prayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by telling what רב did. This story sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the order: רב said קריאת שמע before putting on תפילין. This detail is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Washed his hands
Put on תפילין
Prayed (said שמונה עשרה)

phrases.english: Rav washed his hands,
and recited Shema,
and put on tefillin and prayed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the order of the morning מצוות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's practice: washing, then קריאת שמע, then תפילין, then תפילה.

steps.title: Challenge from the grave-digger ברייתא: תפילין before שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב could do this. A ברייתא about a man digging a grave says he washes, puts on תפילין, and only then says קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? But a ברייתא teaches: One who digs a burial niche for a dead person in the grave is exempt from קריאת שמע, from prayer, from תפילין, and from all מצוות in the Torah. When the time for קריאת שמע arrives, he comes up, washes his hands, puts on תפילין, recites קריאת שמע, and prays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's order from Step 21. It quotes a ברייתא that puts תפילין before קריאת שמע. The גמרא first tries an answer in step 26, and gives its final answer in step 33.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's order is: wash, תפילין, קריאת שמע, pray. רב's order put קריאת שמע before תפילין. The challenge is about the order, not about whether to do these מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: How could he do this?
But a ברייתא teaches! (a challenge from a source)
One who digs a burial niche
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The grave-digger's exemption is not the point. The challenge comes from the order at the end of the ברייתא, where תפילין come before קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But it was taught: One who digs a niche for a dead person in the grave —
is exempt from reciting Shema and from prayer
and from tefillin
and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.
When the time for reciting Shema arrives —
he comes up and washes his hands,
and puts on tefillin,
phrases.notes: תפילין come before שמע here

phrases.english: and recites Shema, and prays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's practice from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's order of saying קריאת שמע before putting on תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the order as washing, תפילין, קריאת שמע, prayer. That contradicts רב's order.

steps.title: The grave-digger teaching seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with רב, the גמרא notes that the ברייתא itself looks self-contradictory. The רישא says the digger is exempt from קריאת שמע, but the סיפא says he is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching itself is difficult! The beginning says he is exempt, and the end says he is obligated?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside its question on רב for a moment. It points out that the grave-digger ברייתא from step 22 seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line of the ברייתא says someone digging a grave is פטור from קריאת שמע. Its later line says that when the time for שמע arrives, he climbs out, washes, puts on תפילין and says שמע, so he sounds חייב. Both cannot be true of the same person.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself. The teaching on its own, apart from the outside question.
The first part of a teaching.
The last part of a teaching.
Exempt, not required.
Obligated, required.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question. It is not yet the main question against רב. The גמרא will return to רב in step 25.

phrases.english: This teaching itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: Points to an internal problem in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: the first part says he is exempt,
phrases.notes: The grave-digger is exempt from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: and the last part says he is obligated?!
phrases.notes: He climbs out and says שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side issue inside the ברייתא that was just quoted against רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case seems to receive two opposite rulings: exempt and obligated.

steps.title: Two diggers versus one digger
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved. The סיפא speaks of two people digging, and the רישא speaks of one person digging alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. The end is talking about two diggers, and the beginning is talking about one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question. The two parts of the ברייתא are about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people dig, one can stop to say שמע while the other keeps working, so he is חייב. A lone digger cannot stop his work for the dead, so he is פטור. The ברייתא is consistent after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (Aramaic).
One (Aramaic).
It is not difficult. A standard opening for an answer.

phrases.english: That is not difficult:
phrases.notes: Signals an answer.

phrases.english: the last part is about two diggers,
phrases.notes: One stops while the other continues.

phrases.english: and the first part is about one digger.
phrases.notes: He cannot stop, so he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each part of the ברייתא refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts of the ברייתא seemed to describe the same lone digger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about one digger and the סיפא is about two, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Back to the main problem with רב
steps.stepSummary: With the side issue settled, the גמרא says the ברייתא still contradicts רב's order of תפילין and קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult for רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the challenge from step 22. Whatever the answer to the side question, the ברייתא still puts תפילין before שמע, which is the opposite of what רב did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Resolving the רישא and סיפא did not touch the real problem. In the ברייתא's case where the digger does say שמע, he puts on תפילין first. רב said שמע first and only then put on תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless. Used to return to the main point.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult for Rav.
phrases.notes: Resumes the question from step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side issue of steps 23-24 and returns to the challenge of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's practice of saying קריאת שמע before putting on תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא orders the actions as תפילין first and then שמע, the reverse of רב.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said that עול מלכות שמים comes first and only afterward עול מצוות. That is why רב said שמע before putting on תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said: first accept the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and afterward the yoke of the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. He follows a different opinion, the one of רבי יהושע בן קרחה that we saw earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע is accepting עול מלכות שמים. Putting on תפילין is keeping a מצוה, which is עול מצוות. If accepting God's kingship comes first, then שמע should come before תפילין, just as רב did.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion.
The yoke of the kingdom of Heaven: accepting God as King, expressed by שמע.
The yoke of the commandments: committing to keep the מצוות.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
phrases.notes: Ties רב to an earlier opinion on the דף.

phrases.english: who said: the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven first,
phrases.notes: Accepting God's kingship.

phrases.english: and afterward the yoke of the מצוות.
phrases.notes: So שמע comes before תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 25 by giving רב a source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing רב to a different authority whose principle supports his practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to go against the ברייתא's order with no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב applies רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule, kingship before מצוות, to the order of שמע and תפילין.

steps.title: Reading before reading is not the same as reading before doing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that defense. רבי יהושע בן קרחה only said which passage of reading comes before another passage of reading. He never said that reading comes before actually doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that רבי יהושע בן קרחה said to put one reading before another reading. Putting reading before doing, did you hear that from him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It argues that רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule does not reach as far as רב needs it to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה was explaining why the paragraph of שמע is read before the paragraph of והיה אם שמוע. Both of those are reading. Putting on תפילין is an action (עשייה), and his rule never said reading comes before an action. So רב is not yet defended.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, grant. Concedes a point before limiting it.
To put first, to give priority.
Reading or reciting, here of a passage of שמע.
Doing, actually performing a מצוה.
Did you hear him say so? A rhetorical challenge meaning he never said it.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יהושע בן קרחה was talking about תפילין. He was only talking about the order of the paragraphs of קריאת שמע. That gap is exactly what the גמרא is pointing out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sharpens the line between ordering texts (reading versus reading) and ordering actions (reading versus doing). The sugya never bridges this gap. It drops the רבי יהושע בן קרחה defense and in the end defends רב differently, with the late messenger in step 33.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה —
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said
phrases.notes: Grants his statement, then limits it.

phrases.english: to put one reading before another reading,
phrases.notes: The paragraph of שמע before והיה אם שמוע.

phrases.english: but reading before doing, did you hear him say that?!
phrases.notes: Putting on תפילין is doing, not reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 26 by limiting how far רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן קרחה only ordered one reading before another. רב's case is reading versus an action (תפילין), which his rule does not cover.

steps.title: רב's own practice shows תפילין first, then שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another attack. רב does not seem to hold like רבי יהושע בן קרחה at all, because רב חייא בר אשי often saw רב put on תפילין first and only afterward say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, does רב really hold like רבי יהושע בן קרחה? But רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב. He would first wash his hands, make a ברכה, teach us our lesson, put on תפילין, and only then say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second problem with the idea that רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה. An eyewitness report shows רב doing the exact opposite order: תפילין first, then שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא said רב puts שמע first because קבלת עול מלכות שמים comes before עול מצוות. רב חייא בר אשי's testimony shows רב putting on תפילין, which is a מצוה, before saying שמע. So רב's own regular behavior does not fit that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It introduces an additional challenge.
Many times. This shows it was a regular habit, not a one-time event.
He taught us our lesson (our chapter of learning).
And afterward, and then.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב חייא בר אשי (the eyewitness here) with רבי חייא בר אבא, who appears at the end of this section quoting רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And furthermore, does he (Rav) really hold
like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha?
But didn't Rav Chiyya bar Ashi say:
Many times I was standing
before Rav,
and he would first wash his hands,
make a blessing, and teach us our lesson,
and put on tefillin,
and then he would recite Shema.
phrases.notes: The order is the key point: tefillin come before שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, מִי סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection against the defense in step 26, on top of the objection in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 26) that רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה and therefore puts שמע before תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness reports that רב regularly put on תפילין before שמע, which is the opposite of what that position would require.

steps.title: Maybe it was before the time for שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible defense. Maybe רב put on תפילין first only because the time for קריאת שמע had not yet arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: this was when the time for קריאת שמע had not yet arrived...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a suggested answer to step 28 and is setting up a reply to it. Perhaps רב only put on תפילין first because it was still too early to say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it was too early for שמע, then putting on תפילין first does not show any preference for מצוות over שמע. רב was simply doing what he could do at that moment. This would save the idea that רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It introduces a possible answer that the גמרא is about to reject.
The time arrived.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
it was when the time for reciting Shema had not yet arrived,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בִּדְלָא מְטָא זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a defense against the objection in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a time before שמע could be said.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's story shows he put a מצוה before שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: He put on תפילין first only because it was too early to say שמע.

steps.title: Then why bother reporting the story?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that defense. If רב only put on תפילין first because it was too early for שמע, then רב חייא בר אשי's testimony would teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of רב חייא בר אשי's testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion in step 29. If nothing unusual happened, why would רב חייא בר אשי bother telling us about it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic report about a teacher's conduct is expected to teach something. If the order was only because of timing, the story seems to have no lesson. So the defense seems to empty the testimony of meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If so.
His testimony, his report.

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of the testimony
of Rav Chiyya bar Ashi?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מַאי אַסְהַדְתֵּיהּ דְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the defense offered in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב put on תפילין first only because it was too early for שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the testimony teaches nothing, and a testimony is assumed to teach a lesson.

steps.title: The story teaches that learning משנה needs a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the testimony does have a point. It shows that רב made a ברכת התורה before teaching משנה, which goes against the view that משנה needs no ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the one who says that for משנה one does not need to make a ברכה. It teaches us that even for משנה one must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real lesson of רב חייא בר אשי's story. The point is not the order of תפילין and שמע. The point is that רב made a ברכה before teaching משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now step 30's question is answered: the testimony is meaningful because of the ברכה, not because of the timing. This keeps the defense from step 29 alive: it was simply too early for שמע. The story is about the ברכה on Torah learning.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude. It comes to reject a different opinion.
The one who says (a certain opinion).
It teaches us. It introduces the new lesson.
Must make a ברכה (here, ברכת התורה).

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source that ברכת התורה applies to learning משנה, not only to learning מקרא (written Torah).

phrases.english: To exclude the one who says
that for Mishnah one need not bless,
it teaches us
that even for Mishnah one must also bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמַּאן דְּאָמַר לַמִּשְׁנָה אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30 and so supports the defense in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the purpose of the source to a different lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony is pointless unless it teaches something about תפילין and שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony teaches that one makes a ברכה even before learning משנה.

steps.title: Still, the problem for רב remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main issue. Even after all this, the ברייתא still contradicts רב, who said שמע before putting on תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main problem from step 25, which is still unsolved. The ברייתא still does not match רב's practice of saying שמע before תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side discussion about רב חייא בר אשי's story did not save רב. The defense from רבי יהושע בן קרחה already fell in step 27. So the contradiction between the ברייתא and רב still needs an answer, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless.
It is difficult. A problem remains.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult for Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about the ברכה and returns to the open difficulty of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's practice of saying שמע before putting on תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires תפילין before שמע, and no defense has worked yet.

steps.title: The messenger was late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the difficulty. On that occasion, the messenger bringing רב's תפילין was late, so רב said שמע on time and put on תפילין afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the messenger who was at fault.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer for רב. רב did not choose to say שמע first. His תפילין simply had not arrived yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רב's practice into a one-time situation, not a rule. רב agrees that תפילין should come before שמע. He just did not want to miss the proper time for שמע while waiting for a late messenger.

keyTerms.meaning: The messenger.
Did wrong, was at fault (here, came late).

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רב agrees with the ברייתא that one should put on תפילין before saying שמע. He said שמע first only because his תפילין came late, and he did not want to miss the time.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not learn from רב that saying שמע before תפילין is the preferred order. The גמרא's conclusion is that it was an exception caused by a late messenger.

phrases.english: It was the messenger who was at fault.
phrases.notes: The messenger brought the tefillin late.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty restated in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the event as a special circumstance (בדיעבד), not a rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב holds that שמע should be said before תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds תפילין first. He said שמע first only because the messenger was late.

steps.title: שמע without תפילין is like false testimony
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that saying קריאת שמע without wearing תפילין is like testifying falsely about oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Anyone who says קריאת שמע without תפילין is like someone who gives false testimony about himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins about how serious it is to say שמע without תפילין. עולא compares it to false testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמע a person says 'וקשרתם לאות על ידך', which describes his duty to wear תפילין. If he says this without wearing them, his own words testify against him. This builds on the conclusion that תפילין should ideally be on before שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: עולא, an אמורא who traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל.
False testimony.
About himself, against himself.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּלֹא תְּפִילִּין,
phrases.english: Anyone who recites Shema without tefillin,
it is as if he gives false testimony about himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: כָּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּלֹא תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the conclusion about תפילין and שמע with a new statement on how serious it is to say שמע without תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying שמע without תפילין is like testifying falsely against oneself.

steps.title: שמע without תפילין is like an incomplete offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבי חייא בר אבא, compares saying שמע without תפילין to bringing a קרבן without its required additions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is as if he brought a עולה without a מנחה, and a זבח without נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives a different comparison for saying שמע without תפילין. He compares it to a קרבן brought without the offerings that should go with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עולה brought without its מנחה, or a זבח without its נסכים, still counts. But it is missing something. In the same way, one fulfills קריאת שמע without תפילין, but the מצוה is incomplete. This is softer than עולא's 'false testimony' picture.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח.
A flour offering that accompanies certain קרבנות.
An animal offering (here, a שלמים).
Wine libations poured with a קרבן.

steps.whatToRemember: Both עולא and רבי יוחנן teach that שמע should be said while wearing תפילין. עולא calls it 'false testimony', and רבי יוחנן calls it an 'incomplete offering'. In both views one still fulfills the מצוה of שמע, but in a lacking way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is as if he offered a burnt-offering without a meal-offering,
and a sacrifice without libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב עוֹלָה בְּלֹא מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, parallel comparison to עולא's statement in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying שמע without תפילין is valid but incomplete, like a קרבן missing its accompanying offerings.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן begins describing complete acceptance of Heaven's kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן opens a new teaching about a person who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים שלמה, a complete acceptance of Heaven's kingship.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A person who wants to accept upon himself the complete yoke of the kingdom of Heaven...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי יוחנן. This line only sets up the case of someone who wants to accept Heaven's kingship completely, and the instructions follow next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps warned that saying שמע without תפילין is incomplete. Now רבי יוחנן moves from that warning to the positive side: what a person should do for a complete acceptance of Heaven's rule. The key word is שלמה, 'complete,' which shows that just saying the words of שמע may not be the full ideal.

keyTerms.meaning: The yoke of the kingdom of Heaven: accepting ה׳ as King, mainly through קריאת שמע
Complete, whole
One who wants or seeks
That he should accept upon himself

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. רבי יוחנן's actual instructions for how to do this come in the next line, at the start of the next דף. Do not look for the answer on this amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shapes the ideal order of the morning routine around שמע and תפילה, and it completes the theme of the earlier steps about joining שמע with תפילין.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The word 'And' links this to the earlier teachings of רבי יוחנן in step 35.

phrases.english: One who wants to accept upon himself
phrases.notes: This describes the person the teaching is about.

phrases.english: the complete yoke of the kingdom of Heaven
phrases.notes: 'Complete' is the key word. It points to a full, ideal acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שְׁלֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings linking קריאת שמע and תפילין. It moves from the warnings in steps 34-35 to a positive description of the ideal practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of רבי יוחנן's teaching: it introduces the case of one who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים completely. The practical instructions follow in the continuation.
